discrepancies.title: OM occupancy 98.0% vs rent roll 91.4%

sources.label: OM occupancy (as of as at June 2026)

sources.doc: Al Mehrab Bldg - Tenancy List Sep 2026.pdf
sources.label: rent roll: 64 of 70 units let at 2026-09-30

discrepancies.why: The rent roll is unit-level and dated 2026-09-30; the OM figure (as of as at June 2026) is a headline the screen cannot trace to units. A gap of 6.6 points is about 5 units.

impact.basis: 5 units x average in-place rent AED 106,367 (estimate of income the OM implies but the roll does not show)

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date; reconcile the OM figure to unit numbers.

discrepancies.title: Title not stated; legal check required before any further work

sources.quote: Tenure Title deed in the name of the Seller (land and building)
sources.label: OM title

sources.quote: Transfer is subject to the purchaser meeting Dubai Land Department ownership eligibility for the plot.
sources.label: verified quote

sources.quote: Title deed in the name of the Seller (land and building)
sources.label: verified quote

discrepancies.why: The mandate requires freehold single title; the OM states tenure unstated, ownership single_title. The screen does not decide title; until legal confirms it, nothing else about the deal matters. Review: The OM says transfer depends on the purchaser meeting DLD ownership eligibility for the plot. That points to a plot that may not be open freehold, or that may be restricted by nationality. The tenure line on page 3 says whose name the title deed is in. It does not say freehold or single title. An institutional buyer may not be eligible, which could decide whether the deal fits the mandate.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Obtain the title deed(s) and DLD ownership records; legal to confirm freehold status and any nationality restriction before any further work.

discrepancies.title: Headline net yield is built on figures before any vacancy or collection allowance

sources.quote: Figures before vacancy and collection allowances.
sources.label: verified quote

sources.quote: Net yield on total acquisition cost 5.75%
sources.label: verified quote

discrepancies.why: The 5.75% net yield uses NOI from owner statements with no vacancy or collection loss. The rent roll shows vacant, under-renewal and notice-served units, and the operating statement has no vacancy or collection loss lines. Underwritten NOI and yield would be lower.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Rebuild NOI with a vacancy and collection allowance based on the rent roll, and re-check the yield on that NOI. Ask for bank statements or rent receipts to verify collections.

rejected_model_findings.title: Contracted rent headline sits alongside 98% occupancy while the rent roll shows 6 vacant units

evidence.quote: Gross rental income AED 6,807,500 per annum (contracted)

rejected_model_findings.why: The OM calls AED 6,807,500 contracted income. The rent roll as parsed shows 6 vacant units, yet in-place rent equals potential rent at the same AED 6,807,500. So the headline figure may include rent for units that are not let. If it does, income, NOI and the yield are overstated.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Reconcile the AED 6,807,500 to the Ejari register and the rent roll, unit by unit. Confirm whether vacant units carry rent in the figure. Re-base income on let units only.
rejected_model_findings.rejected_because: contradicted by the rent roll: OM income AED 6,807,500 equals in-place rent AED 6,807,500 within 2%

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
Title not stated; legal check required before any further work. The deal is blocked on title and nothing else matters until legal confirms it.

The mandate verdict is Needs work. It passes the hard tests on asset type, area, unit count, price, building age, Year-1 DSCR and related-party master lease. Title is unknown, which counts as a soft fail. It also misses three soft tests: yield on cost, levered IRR and equity multiple (table below).

Recommendation: do not commit diligence spend until title clears. Even then, only pursue at or below the walk-away price of AED 63.51m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], a 15.88% [[uw.walk_away_discount_to_asking]] discount to the AED 75.50m [[deal.asking_price_aed]] asking price. The target return sets that price.

## The deal
- Al Mehrab Building, Al Barsha 1, behind Mall of the Emirates. Built 2009 [[deal.completion_year]], G+M+6, 70 units [[om.unit_count]].
- Asking AED 75.50m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], or AED 886 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA.
- Direct leases, no master tenant. In-place rent is AED 6.81m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. Occupancy by units is 91.43% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] at 30 September 2026 [[rr.as_of]], with 6 vacant units [[rr.vacant_units]]. The landlord pays the chiller.

## Returns and key metrics
| Metric | Screen | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Year-1 NOI | AED 4.68m [[uw.noi_year1]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.83% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.00% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum |
| Year-1 DSCR | 1.48x [[uw.dscr_year1]] | 1.30x [[mandate.min_dscr_year1.threshold]] floor |
| Levered IRR (pre-tax) | 0.93% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] | 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]] |
| Equity multiple (pre-tax) | 1.04x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.35x [[mandate.target_equity_multiple.threshold]] |

The OM headline yield is 5.75% [[om.yield_stated]], net on total cost. On the buyer's basis it is 5.83% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The OM's own income reproduces at 5.74% [[uw.om_yield.reproduced_on_om_basis]]. The yield is not overstated, but the OM builds it with no vacancy or collection allowance, and it still misses the mandate.

## What would make it fail
- **Exit.** Gross exit value is AED 71.10m [[uw.gross_exit_value_aed]], below the purchase price. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, levered IRR is -4.18% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]]. Even with rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, it is only 5.66% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.levered_irr_pre_tax]], short of 8.00% [[mandate.target_levered_irr.threshold]].
- **Rollover.** The largest expiry window holds 25.98% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of rent, AED 1.77m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]], between 30 September 2026 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 29 December 2026 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. That is inside the concentration limit. But the underwriting assumes market rent falls 4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1, and the Al Barsha market rent reference is unverified.
- **Over-renting.** 9.97% [[uw.over_rent_share_of_income]] of income comes from units let above the market reference, so those rents may reset down at renewal.
- **Occupancy.** The OM says 98.00% [[om.occupancy_stated]]; the rent roll shows 91.43% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]]. Debt cover is the cushion: it stays at 1.43x [[uw.sens.r-5.e+0.dscr_year1]] with rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower, and Year-1 NOI covers debt service down to 73.70% [[uw.breakeven_occupancy_dscr_1]] occupancy. The problem is the return, not solvency.

## Discrepancies that matter
1. **Title (high).** The OM gives tenure as unstated and ownership as single title. It also says transfer depends on the purchaser meeting DLD ownership eligibility. That points to a plot that may not be open freehold, or may carry a nationality restriction. An institutional buyer may be ineligible. The screen relied on no source and does not decide title.
2. **Occupancy (high).** The OM says 98.00% [[om.occupancy_stated]] as at June 2026 [[om.occupancy_as_of]]. The unit-level rent roll, dated later, shows 91.43% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]]. The screen relied on the rent roll because it can be traced to units. The implied income the roll does not show is about AED 532k [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.impact_delta_aed]] a year.
3. **OM yield build (medium).** The OM yield uses owner-statement NOI with no vacancy or collection loss, although the roll shows vacant, under-renewal and notice-served units. The screen relied on the documents and added allowances, so true NOI is lower than the OM implies.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Before diligence, check
- Title deed(s) and DLD ownership records. Legal confirms freehold status and any nationality restriction first.
- Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date, reconciled to the OM occupancy.
- Bank statements or rent receipts to verify collections, and owner statements rebuilt with vacancy and collection allowances.
- Independent verification of the Al Barsha market rent reference.

## Assumptions
Leverage is 45.00% [[assume.ltv]] LTV at 6.80% [[uw.interest_rate]] (3M EIBOR 4.30% [[assume.eibor]] plus a 2.50% [[assume.margin]] margin), amortising over 20 years [[assume.amortisation_years]]. Structural vacancy is 5.00% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss 1.00% [[assume.collection_loss]]. Exit yield is 7.00% [[uw.exit_yield]] after the 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] expansion assumption, with a 5-year [[uw.hold_years]] hold from 1 January 2027 [[uw.analysis_start]]. Market rent moves -4.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1, -1.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then 2.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.00% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. The package supplied the full operating statement, so no cost lines came from mandate defaults.
